title: Full Plaintext Recovery for XCB
summary: Separate attacks recover A in three queries and B in four; the recorded unresolved task is to recover their full concatenation with one attack.

formal_statement.body: In attacks on XCB, one attack uses three queries to recover plaintext component $A$, while another uses four queries to recover component $B$. Determine whether an attack can recover the full concatenated plaintext $A\mathbin{\|}B$.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptanalysis of XCB plaintext-recovery attacks.
parameters: A and B: plaintext components whose concatenation forms the full plaintext
Three queries: stated cost of the attack recovering A
Four queries: stated cost of the attack recovering B
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether an attack can recover the complete plaintext formed by concatenating A and B.

citations.label: How to Recover the Full Plaintext of XCB

progress.summary: The source poses full plaintext recovery as the next target after separate attacks recover A and B. The supplied surrounding text then answers the question affirmatively.
citation_labels: Peng Wang et al., How to Recover the Full Plaintext of XCB
